column1: # Hand-made place names. A photo taken inside one of these circles is given this
# name instead of the automatic one (see waterfall/places.py).
# One place per line, separated by TABS:
#     name <TAB> country code <TAB> latitude <TAB> longitude <TAB> radius in km <TAB> note (optional)
# The name is shown exactly as written, followed by the country. Where circles
# overlap, the one whose centre is nearest in proportion to its own radius wins,
# so a small circle inside a large one still works.
# These entries were chosen by hand, by someone who knows the places. Each position was
# checked against a second source before it was written down, and the note says which:
# OSM = OpenStreetMap, GN = GeoNames, WP = Wikipedia. Three could not be, and say so:
# two are marked ONE SOURCE and one ESTIMATED. GeoNames alone is not enough here: its
# "Tokeh", "Kent" and "Tombo" all sit on one wrong spot in the middle of Waterloo.
# A long beach, or a place with two parts, is two circles with the same name.
# West coast of the Freetown peninsula, north to south. Beaches carry the word "Beach"; the two towns do not.
